rationale: M59 (#825). Every expected line below is read off the fixture's own text (not off the analyzer's output — the flag above says so rather than claiming an authorship order that did not happen; the values were then checked line by line against live emission before commit). typescript emitted NO line on any relationship before this round: the M59 oracle measured 0 of 2,074 relationships carrying a line on the pinned 40-file sample this round used. The constructs are split across lines so each expect/forbid pair is a DIFFERENT line, which is what makes the contract falsifiable: the `import {` keyword is on 16 while its specifiers are on 17/18; `export class Worker` is on 26 while its base name is on 27; the call chain opens on `helper` (31) but is called on `.doWork()` (33). The forbid entries are exactly the pre-fix answers: no line at all, or the construct's opening line. A WRAPPED `new` (`new\n  Thing()`) is deliberately absent — the pinned grammar does not parse it as a new_expression, so it is a grammar finding (#858), not a line expectation, and pinning it here would encode a wrong answer as the expected one. Symbol lines are pinned through the `contains` edges rather than through `expectSymbols`, because expectation entries match on flat equality (a nested `range` object would never match).
